Two links are missing: the body's function and the law governing that shipment. Scientific assessment evaluates evidence and estimates exposure and effects. Risk management and enforcement use that assessment within their own remit; they are not the same task. Pages 7–10 mix educational explanation, history and terminology. We therefore check present roles against official sources instead of converting an old statement about absence of residues into a universal registration condition. A defined residue limit with conditions is a different proposition from absolute zero.

Quantification limits concern fitness of numerical measurement for an intended purpose. Here LOQ means the lower quantification limit. A result between LOD and LOQ may indicate detection without meeting quantitative requirements. Its actual interpretation depends on the reporting convention and method validation. Do not present it as an unqualified precise measurement, or erase the detected signal merely because it is below LOQ.

parts.spokenText: Bioaccumulation is the broader uptake-and-retention question across exposure routes. Bioconcentration isolates uptake from the surrounding medium, such as water, from dietary uptake. The OECD 305 abstract distinguishes aqueous and dietary exposure and follows uptake and post-exposure loss. Here it anchors the study-design distinction, not permission to conduct an animal experiment. Field observations combining food and water do not automatically constitute a controlled aqueous BCF test.

This relationship has a chemical applicability domain, not automatic validity for metals or unidentified substances. The raw concentration ratio answers a different question and cannot silently replace the normalised one.

parts.spokenText: Kinetics is an outline heading in the source; here we add a bounded teaching model. Assume one compartment, constant water concentration, aqueous uptake only and constant rate coefficients, without separate growth or metabolism terms. Net concentration change is the uptake rate minus the loss rate. The uptake rate is the uptake coefficient multiplied by water concentration; the loss rate is the loss coefficient multiplied by body concentration. The units of k1 are L/kg/day and those of k2 are 1/day. At zero net change, body concentration may remain constant while uptake and loss continue. This kinetic steady state is neither stopped molecular movement nor proof of thermodynamic equilibrium. Under these assumptions steady-state body concentration divided by water concentration equals the uptake coefficient divided by the loss coefficient. Changing water concentrations, important growth or poor model fit prevent unqualified application of this simple result.

The uptake coefficient is twenty litres per kilogram per day, and the loss coefficient is zero point one per day. Multiply by water concentration to obtain a steady-state body concentration of zero point four milligrams per kilogram. Check the fluxes: uptake is twenty times water concentration, while loss is zero point one times body concentration. Both equal zero point zero four milligrams per kilogram per day. Net change is zero, but uptake and loss continue. This is a model result, not a field measurement or toxicity percentage.

parts.spokenText: LC50 links a concentration to 50-percent mortality under a specified test and duration. It is not a body-mass dose or a concentration suitable for all aquatic life. Chronic tests may examine growth, reproduction or survival under defined conditions; duration alone does not make unlike endpoints comparable. NOEC and LOEC depend on the tested concentrations and statistical comparison with controls. They locate the highest tested concentration without, and the lowest with, the specified statistically significant effect under the method. Lack of significance does not establish absence of every effect; concentration spacing, sample size and analysis matter.

parts.spokenText: Use invented values from studies assumed compatible in substance, species and comparison method. NOEC is zero point zero four milligrams per litre and LOEC is zero point one six. Their product is zero point zero zero six four. Taking the square root gives a geometric mean of zero point zero eight milligrams per litre. If the compatible median lethal concentration is zero point eight, dividing it by the geometric mean gives an acute-to-chronic ratio of ten. We have not calculated ten-percent mortality, an operative water criterion or guaranteed ninety-five-percent protection. An arithmetic mean would give a different answer and would not implement the required expression.

parts.spokenText: Kow compares n-octanol and water concentrations at equilibrium under defined conditions. With compatible concentration units the ratio is dimensionless; logKow is its base-ten logarithm. A one-unit logKow difference means a tenfold Kow difference, not an additive increase of one in the ratio. The property informs partitioning questions; it is not a direct BCF, toxicity measure or guarantee of systemic translocation. For ionisable substances, inspect pH, measured form and the coefficient's definition before comparing values. A regression without coefficients and a domain remains incomplete.

parts.spokenText: Two hypothetical logKow values, under compatible conditions, are two for A and three for B. Convert logarithms back to ratios: ten to the power of two equals one hundred. parts.spokenText: Assume a simple model: parent decline rate is proportional to the remaining amount, with constant k and no new input. Then concentration at time t equals initial concentration times the exponential of negative k times t and half-life equals the natural logarithm of two divided by k. The time units of k and t must match. Each half-life halves what remains; it does not remove a constant amount each interval. EPA explains that actual transformation curves need not follow one exponential. DT50, the time to half the initial value, is not necessarily a constant half-life throughout a non-exponential curve. We solve the assumed model, not claim a fit to actual observations.

Eight days contain two half-lives. The first four days leave zero point four; the next four leave zero point two milligrams per kilogram, one quarter of the initial value. Each interval halves the remainder instead of subtracting the same amount. The exponential expression checks the result using a coefficient equal to the natural logarithm of two divided by four days. This is parent decline in an invented model. It establishes neither disappearance of products nor food acceptability or permission to shorten a pre-harvest interval.

parts.spokenText: The figure distinguishes dynamic spreading associated with impact from subsequent static spreading under liquid–surface conditions. It also includes drying, redistribution/weathering, uptake, surface activity and losses. Drying does not mean chemical disappearance; a deposit may remain, move, act at the surface or be lost later. Movement on the plant differs from entry into it, and entry does not establish the intended biological response. A useful presentation separates location, identity, state and effect evidence. Realistic imagery helps only if it preserves those distinctions; a striking shot in which every droplet instantly enters the plant teaches the wrong relationship.

parts.spokenText: Follow a droplet in a teaching scene without presenting it as a measured experiment. It reaches a leaf, strikes it, partly rebounds, and partly remains, spreads and dries. Match arrival with transport, contact with impaction, and the retained portion with retention and deposit formation. Then examine spreading and drying, leaving uptake and biological effect unknown until supported. We have no retained-mass measurement, uptake result or control-efficacy finding. The next question might concern surface mass, its distribution, internal plant residue or a suitable response. If rain is followed by water detection, redistribution becomes a hypothesis to test, not permission to assign the source or invent a loss percentage.
